dedupe_keys.name: cerf dc a python package to evaluate the feasibility and costs of data center siting options

description: The IMMM-SFA team publishes CERF-DC, a Python tool for siting data centres against geospatial constraints and costs. Zenodo archives version 1.0.0 under BSD 3-Clause and links the public repository. The README describes rasters for land cost, electricity tariffs, property tax and suitability, with user-defined minimum campus size and power needs in YAML. A command-line or Python call selects candidate grid-cell clusters and exports site costs and attributes as a GeoDataFrame or GeoJSON. This model supports capacity-planning simulations that compare future data-centre locations and grid-interconnection assumptions. No related catalogue record explicitly covers this package. Coverage is whichever region and cost layers the user supplies, not a fixed global siting recommendation. A limitation is that input raster quality and cost assumptions determine feasibility; environmental permits and actual interconnection approval are not guaranteed. The package was not installed and no suggested site was verified.
